chunks: Hadith 232 — Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Ahwāzī narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, who said:

Al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام said: “When you enter the bathhouse, then say at the time when you remove your clothes: O Allah, remove from me the tether of hypocrisy and make me firm upon faith.
And when you enter the first room, say: O Allah, indeed I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, and I seek Your protection from its harm.
And when you enter the second room, say: O Allah, remove from me filth and impurity, and purify my body and my heart.

And take some of the hot water and place it on your head, and pour some of it over your feet. If it is possible for you to swallow a sip of it, then do so, for it cleanses the bladder. And remain in the second room for a while.

And when you enter the third room, say: We seek refuge in Allah from the Fire, and we ask Him for Paradise—repeating it until the time of your خروج from the hot room. And beware of drinking cold water and al-fuqqāʿ in the bathhouse, for it spoils the stomach.

And do not pour cold water over yourself, for it weakens the body. But pour cold water over your feet when you leave, for it draws illness out from your body. Then when you put on your clothes, say: O Allah, clothe me with taqwa and keep me away from ruin. If you do that, you will be safe from every illness.”

key_terms.التَّقْوَى: God-consciousness or piety, described as a garment to be worn
key_terms.الرِّجْسَ النِّجْسَ: filth and impurity, both moral and bodily impurity in the wording of the supplication
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, from which refuge is sought
key_terms.الْإِيمَانِ: faith, steadfastness upon which is requested from Allah
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise, which is asked from Allah
key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: the bathhouse, the setting in which these etiquettes and supplications are taught
key_terms.رِبْقَةَ النِّفَاقِ: the tether or bond of hypocrisy, from which the supplicant asks Allah to be freed
key_terms.شَرِّ نَفْسِي: the evil of one’s own self, from which refuge is sought

ai.seo_question: What du'as and etiquettes did Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach for entering the bathhouse?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches the etiquette of entering the bathhouse, combining physical cleanliness with du'a, seeking refuge, and remembrance of Allah. It links bodily purification with purification of the heart and faith, and includes practical guidance meant to preserve health and well-being.
